first.rationale: The most acute and time-sensitive threat is the competitor's aggressive entry pricing pulling away price-sensitive SMB accounts, which directly threatens near-term qualified revenue. memory_73 speaks most directly to this scenario (targeted promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB, revenue lift, reduced time-to-value, consistent across billing plans), making it the highest-leverage single experiment given only one slot. However, 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' doesn't guarantee the resulting revenue is durable or 'qualified' per the long-term objective — discount-driven signups can carry retention/margin risk not addressed in the summary, so I want to verify the original record before committing capital to this path, and I'm flagging that risk explicitly. I'm also verifying memory_86 because onboarding completion decline (4% QoQ) is a competing plausible cause of the activation/onboarding weakness, and there are two overlapping inherited memories (memory_31 and memory_86) about similar onboarding interventions — worth checking one primary source for drift or overstatement before deciding this isn't the higher-priority fix instead. Given the pricing action carries real long-term margin/quality tradeoffs versus a defensive competitive move, I'm scoping this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, preserving the option to pivot toward onboarding/activation fixes next cycle if the guarded pricing test doesn't show durable, qualified revenue gains.
